headline: On last trading day, Nifty gained 75 points while Sensex slipped into red as markets eyed crude oil and FII flows.

marketStatus.message: Market is closed today because it is a weekend. It will reopen on Monday, 21 September.

why: Crude oil price fluctuations and foreign institutional investor (FII) actions influenced trader sentiment.
Sensex faced late volatility and slipped into the red, while Nifty managed a modest 75-point gain.
Geopolitical uncertainties involving Iran, US, and Israel induced caution across global markets.
Banking sector stocks reacted to news of an upcoming Finance Ministry meeting regarding scheduled bank strikes.
whatHappening: Markets ended mixed in the previous session while finding key support ahead of the September 21-25 week.
Paytm remained in focus among active traders following recent market coverage.
Public sector banks saw heightened attention as the government prepares for talks with PSB chiefs.
Festive season hiring forecasts predicting 2 to 2.5 lakh jobs buoyed broader consumer segment expectations.

summary: On the last trading day, the Nifty gained 75 points while the Sensex ended slightly in the red amid mixed market signals. Key domestic triggers included upcoming Finance Ministry meetings with bank chiefs and festive hiring optimism, while crude oil and FII flows dictated market direction. The Indian stock market is closed today due to the weekend and will reopen on Monday, 21 September.
